CausalChain: High PCSK9 activity -> Increased degradation of LDL receptor on T cells -> Impaired T cell receptor recycling and reduced T cell activation -> Diminished anti-tumor immune response -> PD-1/PD-L1 blockade alone yields suboptimal efficacy; therefore, inhibiting PCSK9 restores LDLR levels and TCR recycling -> Enhanced T cell function -> Synergistic antitumor effect when combined with PD-1/PD-L1 blockade
Hypothesis: Inhibition of PCSK9 will restore LDL receptor‐mediated T cell receptor recycling and function, thereby enhancing the efficacy of PD‐1/PD‐L1 immune checkpoint blockade in hepatocellular carcinoma.
Abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains a complex and treatment‐challenging malignancy, in part due to heterogeneous oncogenic drivers and an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment. Recent breakthroughs include targeted kinase inhibitors and immune checkpoint blockade, yet durable responses are limited. Emerging evidence indicates that the cholesterol regulatory protein PCSK9, classically known for its role in lipid metabolism, may additionally modulate antitumor immunity by affecting antigen presentation and T cell receptor recycling. We propose that, in HCC, high PCSK9 expression leads to reduced LDL receptor (LDLR) recycling on T cells, impairing TCR recycling and T cell activation. Consequently, PCSK9 inhibition in combination with PD‐1/PD‐L1 blockade might synergistically reverse T cell exhaustion, enhance intratumoral CD8+ T cell function, and improve patient outcomes. This hypothesis lays the groundwork for combining clinically approved PCSK9 inhibitors with immune checkpoint inhibitors in HCC therapy.
